meta.signal: WS2812 NZR 800 kbps from RP2040 PIO (T0H~350ns, T1H~700ns, bit 1.25us, exact crystal-derived timing)
meta.byte_layout: bit7=BS0 of PREVIOUS iteration, bit6=BS1 of PREVIOUS iteration, bit5..bit0=R0..R5 of THIS iteration. Chronological order within iteration i: R0..R5 at 37*i+[1,5,9,13,17,21], BS0 at 37*i+27, BS1 at 37*i+32 (stored in byte i+1 bits 7,6). First byte's bits 7..6 are garbage; the last iteration's BS0/BS1 are lost.
meta.trigger: capture starts at the first rising edge on the signal; sample R0 of iteration 0 lands ~1 cycle after the edge test fell through
meta.checksum: sum of 640 raw capture bytes mod 256
meta.marker_split: 3 + 3 bytes; 48 known marker bits (was 64). Chosen by measurement over the 3+3 / 4+2 / 2+4 candidates: lock success is identical (100% for all three across eps -8..+8% x t0 375-736 ns x 18 payloads, 52488 reference decodes) and no split wins once marker CONTENT is held fixed -- recon/approaches/dev_prod/marker_split_study.py
meta.marker_bytes: HEADER FF AA 65 = sync / bit-period ruler / byte alignment. TRAILER 9A 00 FF = byte alignment / worst-case-ZEROS calibration probe / sync + latch. TRAILER[1] is 0x00, NOT a second bit-period ruler: owner decision 2026-09-07 traded 0x55 for 0x00 on the marker-split study's own controls (+7.0 points of plateau bit-exact reconstruction, t0-p90 tail cut) and on the Gate phase's real-silicon interleaved A/B (+26.7 points of delivery, 71.1% -> 97.8% pooled over 90 paired cells, paired McNemar 25:1, chi2 20.35, p<0.001, 0 wrong either way). The end-of-frame ruler measured NO benefit even under within-capture drift, because the refine stage regresses over whole-burst pulses rather than markers. Frame sizing and the 48 known marker bits are unchanged. Corpora acquired before that date carry trailer 9A55FF and are COMPAT corpora -- see recon/PROD_CLOSURE.md section 13.
meta.payload_layout: DATA(16) || C16_HI C16_LO || C16_HI C16_LO || C16_HI C16_LO = 22 bytes; frame = 3 + 22 + 3 = 28 bytes
meta.crc16: CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no reflection, xorout 0x0000) over the DATA bytes only. Check value CRC16('123456789') = 0x29B1
meta.check_block: the same CRC16 written three times, byte order HI,LO in every copy. The receiver recovers its reference by INDEPENDENT PER-BYTE majority: reference_HI = majority(H1,H2,H3), reference_LO = majority(L1,L2,L3). Per byte position the truth survives as the majority when >=2 of the 3 copies are correct there and remains a candidate when >=1 is, so two copies damaged in DIFFERENT byte positions still give the exact 16-bit reference even though no two 16-bit blocks agree. A byte position with no majority contributes its distinct values as candidates ranked by decode confidence; the references are the cross product, capped at 9 (= 3x3).
meta.crc8: NONE. CRC8 is gone from v2.3 -- it went out with v2.2's 4-byte block. The v2.1/v2.2 sets keep it only as a compat mode.
meta.production_sizing: 48 data bytes + 6 check bytes = 54-byte payload, 60-byte frame = exactly 20 WS2812 LEDs (no pad byte; any surplus wire byte inflates the decoder's whole-burst clock fit ~1.6%/byte -- bench/pad_law.py). The marker trim (8->6 bytes) and the check-block growth (4->6 bytes) are one change: together they hold the frame at 60 bytes.
meta.design_goal: ALMOST ALWAYS EMIT. A refusal loses the frame outright under single-transmission delivery, so the decoder emits even on an imperfect reconstruction PROVIDED the 16-bit check validates the payload. The 16-bit check is what makes that safe: p_trial = R/65536, 256x stronger per trial than the old CRC8, which affords about 131 wrong trials per frame at the <=0.2% wrong-emission target (bench/crc.py fa_budget) where the 8-bit check could not afford one. The measured wrong-emission rate is reported at every step and must never be hidden.
meta.delivery: single transmission: each logical frame goes on the wire exactly once; no repeats, no retries, no acks, no sequence numbers. The --reps captures in this dataset are independent bench acquisitions of the same frame, not protocol repeats.
